name: Shared Valuation Contract
required_scope: Add valuation as-of date, target date, holding period, forecast period, metric period, dividend, share basis, and exit basis to one shared valuation contract.
Separate Price Sensitivity, Base-Case Return, Probability-Weighted Return, and User Internal Return.
Preserve frozen schema 5.0.0 Gate 3 compatibility while requiring schema 5.1.0 for new S09 outputs.
Do not implement the S10 forward business-model driver library.

four_output_acceptance.rule: Available at Gate 3 only when Bear, Base, and Bull implied prices and price changes reproduce; it makes no holding-period or formal-return claim.
Requires a validated dated horizon, controlled forecast/metric/dividend/exit semantics, target-date forward shares, and authoritative Base scenario binding; probability approval is not required.
Requires the Base-Case Return prerequisites plus validated, current, approved probability governance and probabilities totaling 100 percent.
Always DISABLED_PRIVATE_GATE_4_ONLY in the public contract; supplied private values are discarded.

semantic_controls: Valuation as-of date must equal the authoritative market-price date and holding days must reproduce from dated endpoints.
S09 formal forecasts use HOLDING_PERIOD_FORECAST and must begin on the valuation date or next day and end on the target date.
Metric periods must explicitly end at, begin at, or represent a point-in-time value at the target date.
Dividend basis, timing, currency, non-reinvestment treatment, and reviewer ownership are explicit; missing dividend is not zero.
S09 exit basis is limited to the controlled SCENARIO_EXIT_MULTIPLE method and EXIT timing.
Current market capitalization uses reported point-in-time shares; scenario prices may use a separately validated target-date forward share bridge.
Formal output validation binds displayed values to authoritative market price, scenario price, dividend, dates, currency, probabilities, and share basis. A merely self-consistent edited output fails.
Below Gate 3, price and return values are suppressed without making the shared contract internally invalid.
Public Bear and Bull price sensitivities are never used as Gate 4 downside or upside return inputs.
Non-FCF multiple-based metrics require their own positive, dated, currency-matched, evidence-linked, reviewer-owned metric basis.

independent_review_resolution.finding: Self-consistent tampered returns could pass validation.
independent_review_resolution.control: Base and weighted returns are recalculated from authoritative parent inputs and independently compared with every displayed input and result.

independent_review_resolution.finding: Gate 2.5 suppression created an exit-basis validation conflict.
independent_review_resolution.control: Suppressed exit basis receives an explicit SUPPRESSED_BELOW_GATE_3 status and remains self-validating.

independent_review_resolution.finding: Independent delivery QA substituted forward shares into current market capitalization.
independent_review_resolution.control: QA now uses valuation-reported shares for current market cap and validates the forward scenario denominator separately.

independent_review_resolution.finding: Period, dividend, and exit fields lacked economic semantics.
independent_review_resolution.control: Controlled enums and target-date relationship tests were added; free-text labels alone cannot unlock formal returns.

independent_review_resolution.finding: Gate 4 mixed public price sensitivities with formal return inputs.
independent_review_resolution.control: Public sensitivities have separate fields and are null in the return/downside pack.

independent_review_resolution.finding: Scenario integration was unnecessarily restricted to positive normalized FCF and hard-coded USD.
independent_review_resolution.control: The shared multiple scenario accepts a validated generic metric basis and carries the authoritative valuation currency and metric unit.

synthetic_formal_return_fixture.note: Synthetic values verify formulas and controls only; they are not company facts or investment conclusions.

scope_boundary: CROX, AZO, and CRM remain price-sensitivity-only because their stored public demo inputs do not contain a complete validated S09 horizon and target-date forward share bridge.
S09 accepts an explicit generic multiple-based metric basis but does not generate business-model forecasts. Driver selection and forward operating bridges remain S10.
S09 does not add peer, historical, reverse-valuation cross-check governance beyond the existing shared controls; that remains S11.
S09 does not create a fund-specific expected return, hurdle comparison, position size, portfolio action, or trade.

exact_next_starting_point.name: Modular Forward Operating Bridges
exact_next_starting_point.first_action: Freeze the shared forward-valuation driver interface, then implement business-model driver modules and a forward share-count bridge with DRIVER_MODEL_NOT_AVAILABLE as the fail-closed fallback.
